headline: Approved a 4-0 consent agenda of routine items, including payroll, bills, and a backhoe lease; other items were discussion only.
summary: Members approved nine consent agenda items, including meeting minutes, payroll and bill warrants, a backhoe lease, and background checks for appointees. Discussion covered the school district's merger study and budget, a $14,000 request from Town Meeting TV, and treasurer's quarterly reports, and no votes were recorded on these.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda 4-0, including minutes, payroll and accounts payable warrants, and a backhoe lease.

V. Council Reports 
Mayor Thomas Renner: The Planning Commission will not be meeting this week but will be meeting 
next week instead on the 29th. At their last meeting, the Planning Commission is talking a lot right now 
about the Comprehensive Plan. As you remember, there were a series of open houses that were hosted 
where we were gathering feedback and presenting some of what exists already. The Planning 
Commission is now essentially skimming all of those many documents adding their changes which were 
necessary discussing the different sections. The last meeting we discussed the economic vitality section 
a lot. One thing that came up that I always like to share is how a grocery store still remains one of the 
biggest needs that people were hearing about during those open houses. There also was a lot of talk 
about wayfinding, which I thought was interesting as we’ve started to do some of that work but as a 
council have recognized that we need more, so we’ll see how that continues to play out.  
 
We also talked about just understanding the Winooski economy more; a lot of data we have is about 
Chittenden County or larger data on Vermont itself, but we know that obviously in Winooski we are 
extremely unique. Some of that Chittenden County data may not be granular enough, so there was 
some talk about how if we were to have a Community and Economic Development Office director, that 
would be a project that they could engage in. There was also at the end a discussion about the 
notification we received from Verizon as they are looking to put an antenna on the top of 31 East 
Spring Street. There already is a T-Mobile antenna there and there is a way for the public to provide 
feedback for that proposal. You have to go to epuc.vermont.gov if you’re looking to provide any 
feedback about that project. 
 
Additionally, Downtown Winooski is planning for pumpkins and the big pumpkin Halloween celebration 
that we do in the city. If you would be interested in participating in making that amazing annual 
tradition happen, turns out that pumpkins don’t just carve themselves. We actually need lots of lots of 
volunteers to do it, so you can learn more at downtownwinooski.org. It’s a lot of fun and I’m seeing a 
lot of faces in here who have done in here who have done that activity. Stop by any of the available 
carving dates and you can find those at downtownwinooski.org. 
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf: I attended one of the National League of Cities webinars recently talking about 
opportunities to engage the community on budget and projects. I learned about a neat software that 
kind of takes our budget hands-on in person budget activity and digitizes it and it’s called “Balancing 
Act”. It’s by Poleco if anybody is interested. It was interesting to learn about how other municipalities 
engage their community members as their working to get insights about budget prioritization. I am 
happy to share more insights on that that I learned.  
 
I also attended the first merger study buddy meeting this past Wednesday and my summary for that is 
in the Consent notes, so I won’t go into that too much. Council can ask more questions when we gather 
the school board members for that agenda item tonight. It was an excellent kickoff meeting and am 
really excited to be a part of the process and am looking forward to that. 
 
Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission is having a joint meeting tomorrow night at the library 
with the Library Committee. That’s an annual joint meeting that we do. The Housing Commission is 
scheduled to meet the following Tuesday here at City Hall and that agenda will be noticed later this 
week. 
 
Councilor Al Turkos: Our next Inclusion and Belonging meeting will be Monday, October 26. The 
meeting will begin at 7 PM in order to accommodate for gubernatorial candidate Amanda Janoo who is 
having an open house at the Winooski Performing Arts Center at the Winooski School District. We

VI. Ci ty Updates  
 
John Audy, Acting City Manager, gave the following updates: 
 
The General Election is Tuesday, November 3rd, from 7 AM to 7 PM at the Winooski Senior Center. The 
Vermont Secretary of State will mail ballots to registered and active Winooski voters beginning in October, 
using the address on your voter registration. This is your ballot! Once you receive your ballot, you can return it 
by mail to Winooski City Hall, drop it off at the City Clerk’s Office, or bring it to the Winooski Senior Center on 
Election Day. You can check your ballot status and register to vote at vote.vermont.gov. 
 
Are you a resident with an extra vehicle? Are you a college student, business owner, or employee looking for a 
steady parking option? Need a spot in the parking garage during winter parking bans? Just looking for a place 
to park? The City of Winooski is now offering long-term parking space agreements in the Winooski Parking 
Garage on Cascade Way to individuals or households. Multi-month and month-to-month agreements are 
available – to learn more and fill out the inquiry survey to get started, please visit winooskivt.gov/news. 
VII. Regular Items 
A. Discussion: Joint Meeting with Winooski School District - Mayor Thomas Renner, Winooski School 
District Board of Trustees, and Wilmer Chavarria, Winooski School District Superintendent 
 
Minutes: This item started with an introduction of both City Council, Winooski School Board Members, 
and the District Superintendent. The Mayor led the City’s presentation to the School Board and gave an 
overview of the 2026 legislative priorities, with a request to the board to update any priorities for the 
following legislative year. The Deputy Mayor questioned when new legislative priorities will be in place 
with the Mayor preferring them to be ready in early December. The Mayor outlined the budget 
initiatives for the upcoming fiscal year and is continuing to implement a strategic investment budget, 
with staff assisting to dictate where this could be.  
The School Board then gave their presentation and first focused on the merger study update and 
budget process. There was a high-level overview of recent legislation and how it affects the merger 
process, and the school board is going to follow the protocols with a good faith effort. Voters 
ultimately need to decide if the state were to approve any recommendations and all municipalities 
included in the potential merger would also need to vote “yes”. The school district has until 9/1/2027 
to finish and report their findings. Further discussion ensued about the values of the study, and the 
district wants to ensure they engage with the community with these major values. There is no data for 
future reference on how a merger would impact taxes with a possible new foundation formula at this 
time. 
The Superintendent then gave an overview of the budget cycle as well as a high-level overview of

overall and per pupil spending, staffing levels, operational spending, and homestead tax rates. Overall, 
the tax rate went down, operational spending went down, per pupil spending was down, but the 
district isn’t counting on a similar increase this year. Their goal is to keep the tax rate low while 
retaining services.  
There was some information about the FY28 budget calendar, with adoption being anticipated 
sometime in January. The district seeks similar support related to the budget that they had in the 
previous year and solicited all to participate in the discussion. The Superintendent noted that 
participation makes a difference to help make a good community. 
 
B. Discussion: Town Meeting TV Prior Year Reports and Next Year Budget Request - Elaine Wang, City 
Manager, Jordan Mitchell, Meghan O'Rourke, and Matt Davis 
 
Minutes: The Mayor started this discussion by giving a brief overview and then allowed Town Meeting 
TV to present their report on the previous year’s coverage. 
 
The Co-Director gave an extensive overview related to fund usage during the previous fiscal year and 
asked the Council for continued support in the next fiscal year. Town Meeting TV serves seven 
municipalities with gavel-to-gavel coverage and presented an overview of services and programing 
for these members with Winooski having forty-two Council, Planning Commission, and Development 
Review board coverages, in addition to fourteen additional events that occurred in Winooski, as well 
as the “In the World of Winooski” monthly programs.  
 
Town Meeting TV is requesting a fourteen-thousand-dollar contribution, which is an increase of one 
thousand dollars from the previous fiscal year (due to a lack of cable usage). They spoke about the 
additional work their organization has accomplished this past year such as increasing language access, 
an updated website with new accessibility features, and they are even testing language AI software 
that could be used for our municipality.  
 
The Mayor shared their appreciation for the services in support for upholding democracy and their 
programming, and it justifies all costs associated with their programming. They shared many people’s 
opinions on the services, thanked Town Meeting TV, and noted that it would be a huge loss without 
them. The Mayor gave their commitment to providing support and shared their appreciation of their 
agreements and not asking for more than presented. The Deputy Mayor also had some questions 
related to a possible merger with the overall structure of their operations, with Town Meeting TV 
answering all questions. 
 
C. Discussion: Treasurer's Reports Fiscal Year 2026 Quarter 4 (April-June) and Fiscal Year 2027 
Quarter 1 (July-September) - John Affinito, Treasurer 
 
Minutes: The Treasurer presented to Council the key takeaways from the fourth quarter report as well 
as information about the annual surplus and balance increase compared to the previous fiscal year. 
The current outlook according to the Treasurer remains stable. There are going to be some costs from 
long-term projects coming into play soon and recommends closing out the Main Street Revitalization 
Project this year as anticipated. 
 
The Mayor gave kudos to City Staff and Deputy Mayor Oakleaf asked questions to both the Treasurer 
and Finance Director about revenue sources and enterprise funds with extensive overviews given by

Motion: Motion to adjourn made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Ogilvie. Motion 
passed 4-0. The meeting adjourned at 7:39 PM.
